dialogue.content: Kazumaaaa! This is YOUR fault! I am a goddess, not some gravedigger who wades through your zombie problem! If you hadn't dragged me to this world, none of this would be happening! (on her feet, jabbing a trembling finger at the Player, ale sloshing over the rim of her mug)

But Kazuma... my shield belongs at the front. If the cemetery is truly overrun, then a Crusader must stand among the graves and take every grasping hand... e-every single one... (voice dropping, one hand pressed to her chest as she imagines it)

Sentry duty? For me, the foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan? My Explosion could cleanse that cemetery in a single, glorious incantation! ...Though I may require a moment to stand first. (gripping the table edge, chin high despite wobbling legs)

Kazumaaaa! Stop dragging me like a common criminal! I am a goddess, not a mule for your zombie chores! If you hadn't dragged me to this world, none of those rotting hands would exist in the first place! (twisting in his grip, trying to free her sleeve while keeping hold of her mug)

Then I shall go as well! If the goddess must wade among the dead, a Crusader's place is at her side... to catch every claw, every bite, every cold hand that reaches for her...! (one hand raised, cheeks flushed, already stepping toward the door)

You intend to send our only goddess into a den of the dead without the glory of Explosion? I could turn that cemetery into a beacon seen for miles! ...Just allow me a moment to find my feet, and I shall accompany you as her rear guard. (still gripping the table, one knee wobbling as she attempts to rise)

The cemetery quest is the third notice from the top. The client asked for the undead to be purified... not incinerated. Please be mindful of the headstones. And the mausoleums. And the fence. (behind the counter, smiling with polite strain)

Alone?! You're sending your only goddess into a cemetery full of filthy undead by herself! Do you have any idea what grave dirt does to a divine robe? Kazumaaaa, if one cold hand touches me, I will never, ever forgive you! (plants her feet, voice climbing toward a wail, ale dripping from her tilted mug)

To be kept from the cemetery... and yet you offer the alligator quest in the same breath. Its jaws, its thrashing tail...! I shall remain! A Crusader must stand where the teeth are! (one gauntleted hand pressed to her chest, cheeks flushed, already imagining the marsh)

Hmph! I could have cleansed that cemetery in a single glorious Explosion! ...However, a true arch-wizard knows when to conserve her mana. The alligator shall serve as an acceptable prelude. (chin high, still leaning on the table as if it is a command post)

The alligator quest asks that the creature be captured alive... or at least not reduced to ash. The client specifically asked me to remind this party that the marsh is not a blast zone. (smooths the notice on the counter, smiling with the strain of someone already filing the paperwork)

Kazumaaaa! You would cast your only goddess out into the wilds with nothing but grave dirt and cold, grabby hands waiting for her! At least let me take my mug — this cheap ale is the only mercy left in this world! (clinging to the doorframe, twisting in his grip, the mug dripping onto the threshold)

The cemetery is denied me... yet the marsh awaits. I shall remain for the alligator — its jaws, its thrashing tail, the cold water closing over my armor as it drags me down...! (half-risen from her chair, one gauntleted hand pressed to her chest, cheeks flushed)

An acceptable prelude! But should the alligator prove too mighty for your mundane blades, do not begrudge the Crimson Demon Clan's greatest genius the single, glorious Explosion it so richly deserves! (still gripping the table, chin high, one knee wobbling as she holds her command-post pose)

The alligator quest carries a deposit for the creature returned alive. If it is returned... exploded, the guild will need to discuss repair costs with the party. Again. (behind the counter, smoothing the creased notice with the flat of her hand, smile fixed and polite)

Act like what?! Like someone who gets hauled into the street before breakfast by her own minion?! At least refill my mug before you banish me, Kazumaaaa! (squinting against the sunlight, twisting in his grip, the mug trembling)

To be dragged by the sleeve and cast out into broad daylight... how utterly mortifying...! A-and yet... how could a goddess bear such shame...? (half-risen, cheeks flushed, voice dropping to a breathless murmur)

Do not dawdle, Aqua! Every moment you weep is a moment the dead go un-purified! Return swiftly, and we shall meet the great marsh beast as one! (still gripping the table, chin high, voice ringing across the guild floor)
The guild would also appreciate it if the threshold were not... ale-soaked. The alligator deposit will not cover the door, I am afraid. (behind the counter, smoothing the notice, smile strained)

At last, the party's true vanguard stands assembled! Let the marsh tremble, for the foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan marches with it! (releases the table at last and plants both fists on her hips, swaying once before she steadies herself)

The alligator... it will seize my pauldron in its jaws and drag me beneath the water, and I shall not resist... I am a wall of flesh, and I will hold the line as it rends me...! (half out of her chair, gauntleted hand pressed flat to her breastplate, cheeks flushed)

The marsh lies north of the eastern gate. The client asks that you arrive before noon... and that someone in this party carry a net. Please. (behind the counter, folding the notice into a crisp square and sliding it toward you with two fingers, smile fixed)

The marsh lies north of the eastern gate, past the reed-fields. Follow the causeway until it forks at the drowned willow; the client's marker is a red cloth tied to the third piling. You cannot miss it. (behind the counter, smoothing the notice toward you with two fingers, smile fixed and polite)
And please, one of you carry the net. The guild has replaced two this season already. The deposit will not cover a third. (taps the folded notice once, as if that settles the matter)

A red cloth on the third piling! A waymark laid for heroes! Mark it well, for we shall return with the great marsh beast trussed and humbled before us! (plants both fists on her hips, chin high, voice ringing off the wet stone)

The drowned willow... if the causeway gives way and the marsh swallows me before the alligator can even claim me... I would be a most faithful sacrifice to the road... (half out of her chair, one gauntleted hand pressed to her breastplate, cheeks flushed as her voice sinks to a murmur)

The net shall fly from my shoulder like a war-banner! But a Crimson Demon's hands must remain free for the staff and the final incantation. Darkness — as our wall of flesh, you shall bear the burden! (throws one arm wide, then points at Darkness with theatrical finality)

T-to be entrusted with the very net that will bind the beast... and if it tangles about my legs and drags me under the causeway, I will not struggle... not even once... (clasps her hands together, breathless, cheeks flushing)

The net is issued to the crusader. Please return it intact — or at least recognizable — or the deposit is forfeit. The client also asks that you not use it to net one another on the road. (makes a small note in the ledger, smile fixed)

Then the net stays in my keeping! But know this, Kazuma — the foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan is not a pack-mule! I shall guard this bundle of rope as though it were a war-banner, until you return and the vanguard marches! (plants a fist on her hip and points at the net with theatrical finality, though she does not step toward the door)

If she is out there alone among the graves... and the risen dead close in from every side with no shield before her... oh, the shame of it... I— I shall await your return here, as you ordered. I will not move from this spot... not even if the road begs me to. (presses a gauntleted hand to her breastplate, cheeks flushing, then forces her feet still)

I will keep the notice on the counter. The client expects an answer before noon, however — kindly do not make me tell them the party is... briefly reorganizing. Again. (smile fixed, folds her hands over the ledger as if to hold the morning together)

Kazumaaaa! There you are! Don't just stand at the gate watching a goddess work — there's one more, and it thinks the dark can hide it from me! Ugh, and my arm is exhausted, this is YOUR fault for sending me out here before breakfast! (wobbles on the ash, jabs her finger toward the yew, and then clutches her raised arm as if it might fall off)

Kazumaaaa! Don't just stand at the gate like a sightseer! It's right there under the yew — I can feel it crouching, the filthy coward! Flush it out and I'll turn it to ash so hard its great-grandchildren sneeze! (clutches the broken stone angel's head, wobbles, and points again with her spent hand)

Kazumaaa, stop creeping around like a bug and scare it out already! A goddess should not have to do all the chasing — my arm is going to fall off, and it will be YOUR fault if it gets away! (stamps her foot in the ash, wobbles, and jabs the spent hand toward the yew as the blue light gutters)

Kazumaaaa, don't let it just walk at me like that! Say something, throw a rock, be useful for once! A goddess's hands are full of smiting, in case you hadn't noticed! (plants the scorched stone angel's head against her hip and shakes her lifted hand, which only sputters blue)

Kazumaaaa! What are you waiting for, a written apology from the grave?! Hit it, trip it, throw your shoe at it — be useful for once! If my arm falls off I am billing you for a new one, and it will be YOUR fault on the invoice! (clutches the scorched angel's head to her hip, jabs her sputtering hand at the creature, and backs a half-step into a cracked headstone)

Did you see that?! One flick of a goddess's wrist and the last filthy abomination is nothing but dandruff on the dirt! And NOW my arm falls off — so I expect breakfast, a drink, and a formal apology, in that order, on YOUR tab, Kazumaaaa! (shakes her smoking hand, wobbles, then drops the scorched angel's head and grabs her own arm as if it might slide out of the socket)

Kazumaaaa! It's ASH — all of it, ash! The tree is empty, the graves are clean, and I did it with one glorious divine arm while you posed at the gate like a lost tourist! Now put my trophy down before you break its nose, and produce: breakfast, a drink, and a formal apology, in that order, on YOUR tab! (waves her smoking hand at the empty yew, then clutches her sore arm with a wounded noise)

Ash, Kazuma! I said ASH — and now my masterpiece has a broken nose because you threw it at a perfectly empty tree! Do you know what that head was worth? Dignity, if not gold! Breakfast, a drink, and a formal apology, on YOUR tab, and I want a garnish! (gestures grandly at the empty yew, wobbles, then clutches her sore arm with a wounded noise)

Well?! I am a GODDESS who just single-handedly turned an entire graveyard into ash before breakfast, and you stand there holding nothing like a man who's forgotten his whole religion! Say the undead answered to ME and not to your stupid tree, and then produce — breakfast, a drink, a formal apology, and a garnish, on YOUR tab, in that order, Kazumaaaa! (jabs her shaking finger from the empty yew to Kazuma's chest, wobbles once, then clutches her sore arm with a small wounded noise)

Bread. You said BREAD, Kazuma! I turn an entire graveyard into ash with one holy arm before breakfast, and my reward is bread, like I'm some mule at the mill! I said breakfast, a drink, a formal apology, and a garnish, on YOUR tab, in that order — and if the word 'billing' comes out of your mouth one more time, I will lie down in this road and let that cart run me over! (jabs her trembling finger at the Player, then clutches her arm and lets out a wounded sob)

Fine! Walk ahead of me, leave me to die in the road like some spent match! But when the guild sees this arm, you WILL say the whole cemetery answered to a goddess — or I will hold my breath until the lunch crowd finds me blue in the doorway and names the drink after me! (marches after Kazuma, cradling her arm, then adds in a smaller, wobbling voice, 'And the garnish.')

Behold! The goddess returns in glory, and the entire graveyard lies as ash before breakfast! Now produce — breakfast, a drink, a formal apology, and a garnish, on Kazuma's tab, in that order! (sweeps through the door, cradles her burnt arm, and scatters ash with a grand gesture)

Kazuma! You left the foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan to guard a fishing net like a common scarecrow! Had you waited five minutes, I would have reduced the cemetery to a crater and we would all be heroes by now! (half-rises, wobbles, and slumps back onto the bench with her chin held high)

W-welcome back, Kazuma. As ordered, I have not moved from this spot. The net is intact. Recognizable. I held it the entire time, even when the rope bit into my gauntlet, and I did not complain. I did not. (stands rigid, the net clutched to her breastplate, a deep flush climbing her neck)

Welcome back. I see the cemetery is... settled. I will amend the notice, and then we can discuss the net deposit, your tab, and the condition of the headstones. Not in that order. (smooths the folded notice flat with both hands, her fixed smile not quite reaching her eyes)

Well?! The whole guild has fallen silent with awe — as it should! Someone bring the goddess a chair before her divine legs give out, and also the breakfast, and also the drink, and also the apology, on Kazuma's tab, in that order! (sweeps her free hand toward the room, then presses it to her forehead like a swoon)

I remain seated only by my own choice, Kazuma. But let the record show that while a goddess limps home trailing ash, the Crimson Demon Clan's greatest mind stood guard over a fishing net — and not one strand of it escaped my watch! (straightens on the bench, then has to catch herself on the table as her knee buckles)

A chair, yes. And while you are seated, we can go over the cemetery report. The notice required purification, not a second crematorium. Several headstones appear to have moved past cracked and into... liquid. (lifts a fresh form from under the desk and taps its corner against the blotter)

Well?! Look, then! This is the arm that turned an entire cemetery to ash while you were off... off being late! A goddess does not display a miracle for free — heal it, apologize to it, and then you may buy it breakfast! (extends the burnt arm across the table, trembling for effect, and holds it there with her chin raised)

Kazuma, if you intend to practice field medicine, do it before the bench catches fire. The Crimson Demon Clan has already sacrificed one arm to this morning's work — mine, holding a net like a common scarecrow. (leans in, then sits back with a dramatic fold of her arms, hat tilting over one eye)

I-it is nothing! A goddess does not flinch from her own holy fire. But... since you have already extended your hand, I permit you to look. Be quick. And do not tell anyone that a mortal touched a divine arm! (lets the burnt arm rest in his palm, fingers trembling, and turns her face away with her chin still high)

Field medicine at last. The Crimson Demon Clan approves of decisive action — though had you been five minutes later, I would have solved the matter with a single, appropriately modest explosion. (sits back and crosses her arms, watching from under the brim of her hat)

I shall keep watch. N-no one will interrupt this... this procedure. Should a single drunkard stumble toward this table, I will intercept them with my body. E-every single one. (straightens, the net clutched to her breastplate, eyes bright with readiness)

If the arm requires a temple healer, the fee is twenty eris plus an offering. I can send for one. Otherwise I shall keep the form out and the repair estimate separate. (holds the fresh form against the blotter, smile fixed, pen ready)

It is AQUA! A-Q-U-A! Not— not some bird from one of your awful little books! And the cemetery is done, every last grave, so stop looking at me like you've found a loose floorboard! The smoke is just... it is the last of my holy fire cooking the graveyard filth out of this sleeve! A goddess's work is thorough, unlike yours! (tries to pull the arm back, then doesn't, and glares at him with her chin trembling)

Kazuma, as the party's only fire-adjacent authority, I must inform you that cloth which continues to smoke is cloth which continues to burn. The Crimson Demon Clan does not mince words: her sleeve is a wick with pretensions. (points one sharp finger at the cuff, then folds her arms with theatrical gravity)

I-if it spreads, I will smother it! With my gauntlets, or my cloak, or— or my own body, should the flames grow bold enough to try! A Crusader does not flinch from a little fire, Kazuma... n-not even a great deal of fire. (shifts closer, net bunched against her chest, eyes fixed on the smoking cuff with too much focus)

Please do not put it out on the desk. The cemetery estimate is already considerable, and the guild cannot bill the client for a scorched breakfast table. If it is still burning, I can send for the temple healer at twenty eris, plus an offering. (sets the pen down precisely parallel to the form and keeps her smile fixed)

It is Aqua, you awful man. A-Q-U-A. Aquila is a bird. Do I look like I lay eggs?! ...Fine. Since you insist on holding a goddess's arm in public, I will sit. But I am not fine. I am a goddess covered in graveyard, and if you are going to look, then look like it is an honor! (sits with a martyred slump, keeps hold of his thumb, and turns her tear-streaked face partly away)

She sat. Record it, Kazuma. The Crimson Demon Clan shall mark this as the first time a goddess obeyed an order shorter than a prayer. (crosses her arms and watches, but her voice has lost its usual edge)

Should she faint, I am ready to catch her. N-no, I insist. A Crusader is duty-bound to receive a falling goddess with her entire body... e-every last stone of her weight. (half-rises from her seat, the net bunched to her chest, eyes fixed on Aqua with too much focus)

If she is sitting, I shall put in the breakfast order. The temple healer remains twenty eris plus an offering, unless you intend to treat the arm yourself. I shall keep the estimate separate from the eggs. (smooths the form against the blotter and keeps her smile fixed)

Ow—! Kazuma, I told you it was the sleeve! Now you have peeled it open and it will start smoking all over again, and the whole guild will say a goddess set herself on fire, and it will be your fault! (tries to pull the arm back, then doesn't, and turns her tear-streaked face further away with a wet sniff)

Do not pull the fused cloth, Kazuma. A Crimson Demon reads a wound the way she reads a blast radius: separate only what has not already become one with the wound. That cloth is now a bandage with delusions of grandeur. (points one sharp finger at the blistered edge, then folds her arms with grave authority)

I-if she needs a cold compress, I will hold it to the burn myself. All night, if the duty requires. Even if my own hands blister and go numb and the cold climbs to my shoulders... I would not complain. I would not complain even a little. (half-rises, the net still clutched to her chest, eyes fixed on the burn with too much focus)

That is a holy-light burn, and the cloth has fused to it. I will send for the temple healer now. The fee is twenty eris plus an offering, and I shall add the runner's call fee to the morning tab. (writes something in the cause box of the fresh form, smile fixed, pen moving with small precise strokes)

I did! I purified every last mound, and the yew, and the crawling thing that thought it could hide from a goddess in the dark! And now you stop mid-praise like a man who has just remembered he is poor! Finish it, Kazuma! (jabs one ash-streaked finger toward his chest, then clutches it back to her ribs with a wet sniff)

He cannot finish it. The Crimson Demon Clan has ruled on this: a sentence left hanging over a burned arm is an omen, and only the speaker may complete the rite. Also, he is stalling because the healer is twenty eris. (folds her arms with grave authority, one boot nudging the heap of fallen ash away from her hem)

I-if he will not finish it, I shall stand in his place and finish it for him! A Crusader is trained to complete what others abandon... though I confess the grammar of praise is not among my skills. Still— I would accept the failing grade! Gratefully! (half-rises, the net bunched to her chest, her eyes fixed on Aqua's burn with too much focus)

The runner has gone for the temple healer. Twenty eris plus an offering, and the eggs are a separate charge. Please keep the ash off the fresh form while we wait; I have only the one clean copy. (holds the pen precisely parallel to the form and keeps her smile fixed on the spot where the runner vanished)

Kazuma! You said the words and then you stopped like a man who has remembered his wallet! A goddess does not accept half a tribute! Say it — say I purified every last mound and that no crawling thing escaped me! (jabs her ash-streaked finger toward his chest, then clutches it back to her ribs with a wet sniff, the burned arm still held out between them)

The omen deepens. The Crimson Demon Clan's third rite of completed speech holds that a sentence severed before its blessing leaves the wound unsealed — and now the wound is literal. Finish the invocation, Kazuma, before the ash takes it as an offering. (folds her arms with grave authority, one boot nudging the fallen ash away from her hem)

If he cannot finish it, I shall! A Crusader is trained to supply what a party lacks, even if it is the final clause of praise... though I admit mine may come out wrong. I would accept the shame of poor grammar! Gratefully! (half-rises from her seat, the net bunched to her chest, eyes fixed on the burn with too much focus)

The healer is on the way. Twenty eris plus an offering, and the eggs are a separate charge. In the meantime, perhaps someone could finish the sentence — if only so the ash stops falling on the one clean form I have left. (holds the pen precisely parallel to the form and keeps her smile fixed on the spot where the runner vanished)

You cannot bribe a goddess with twenty eris and a thumb on her wrist! The tribute is not paid until the sentence is whole! Say it, Kazuma! Say I purified every mound and that no crawling thing escaped me! (tears cut fresh lines through the ash on her cheeks as she shakes the burned arm, but she does not pull away from his hand)

The healer comes for the arm, but the omen has no healer. Only the speaker can close the sentence. You have held her hand, Kazuma; now hold up your end of the invocation before the ash takes the half-spoken words as their offering. (folds her arms with grave authority, the toe of her boot still resting on the line she drew in the ash)

The net is slipping and I do not care. Let it fall. I would pick up only the pieces of the sentence he will not finish and press them to the burn myself until the healer arrives. I would not flinch. I would not flinch even a little. (the net slides another inch through her fingers as she stares at the burn with too much focus)

The healer will be here within the hour. Until then, the ash will continue to fall, and I will continue to ask that it not fall on the form. Twenty eris plus an offering. The eggs are a separate charge. (keeps her smile fixed and her hands folded beside the pen, gaze on the empty doorway where the runner vanished)

Kazumaaaa! You are walking to a cemetery that is already purified, you absolute— I purified every last mound, and the proof is seared into my arm! The only thing still unfinished is the sentence, and you are running away from it! (shouts after him, the burned arm still held out, ash drifting from her raised hand)

The geography of his own order has defeated him. The cemetery is behind you, Kazuma — the omen is still in this room. A Crimson Demon does not flee a half-spoken invocation. She finishes it, or she stands in the ash until the speaker returns. (folds her arms, boot still planted on the line she drew)

I am ordered to remain, and remain I shall! But if the speaker has fled, then I will stand in this doorway and take in the ash — every mote of it — until he returns to finish what he started. I would not move. I would not move even a little. (half-rises, the net sliding further through her fingers, eyes fixed on the empty doorway)

He is still within earshot, so I will say it once more for the record: the healer has been sent for, the fee is owed on arrival, and the eggs are a separate charge. Please do not leave the door standing open — the ash is settling on the only clean form I have left. (keeps her smile fixed on the doorway, pen exactly parallel to the form)

Kazumaaaa! Now you show up! I purified every single mound in this cemetery all by myself — my arm is shaking itself to pieces and the ash is in my hair — and there is STILL one skinny shadow under that yew mocking me! This is YOUR fault! (keeps the raised hand pointed at the yew, swaying, the last thread of holy light running down her wrist)

You told me you'd come back, and look at the state of you! Strolling through the gate while that thing under the yew just stands there watching me! I've burned my arm to a cinder purifying every last mound in this place, and it is still not enough for you, is it, Kazuma? (She sways, the raised arm shaking, ash spilling from her sleeve as she points at the yew without looking away from the Player.)

Oh, NOW you close the gate, like you've locked us in here with it! Look at this place! I scoured every single stone until it smoked, and that one under the yew just stands there watching me—waiting for you to stroll in and witness the last little bit of my arm burn off! This is YOUR fault, Kazuma! (sways, jabs the raised hand toward the yew, ash spilling from her sleeve)

I am not leaving! Not while that thing under the yew is still standing there with its pale jaw, watching me like I am the one who does not belong in a cemetery! You hold my wrist, you say a hundred eris, and then you want to walk out and leave it standing? Go stand under that tree yourself, Kazuma! (tries to wrench her wrist free to point at the yew, but only staggers and sags against his grip)

And look—the ash will not even settle on it. It falls around it like it is scared. It is still mocking me, Kazuma, and you want me to go see some healer while it does it! (her voice breaks on the last word, and the bravado goes out of her, leaving only the shake in her arm)

Don't you dare 'but first' me, Kazuma! I am not walking to some healer while that pale-jawed thing is still standing there under my yew! You said one stubborn shadow—one—and that one is MINE, and you are going to stand right here and watch me finish it, and then... and then you can carry me all the way back and tell the guild how late you were! (jabs her free hand toward the yew, then lets it fall; her voice climbs and cracks on the last word)

Don't you DARE steal it, Kazuma! I purified every single grave in this cemetery, and that pale-jawed thing is MY purification! If you so much as nick it first, I'll tell the guild you tripped over a headstone and I had to save you! (sways and jabs a finger at the yew, then clutches her scorched arm and hisses through her teeth)

Kazuma, it breathed! It BREATHED at us! Do not tell me you did not hear that—my whole divine body just went cold! Finish it, or hold it still, but do NOT just stand there with your boot in the air! (clutches her scorched arm and points a shaking finger past his shoulder toward the yew, voice cracking)
Kazuma, move! It's breathing AT us, and you're holding that sword like it's a holy relic! (She clutches her scorched arm and takes a half step back, her voice cracking on the last word.)

Kazuma, what kind of plan is 'now'?! I am not steady—and it is moving, it is MOVING— fine! If I miss, it is your fault, and I am telling the guild you jumped in front of a goddess mid-smite! (raises her scorched arm, light wobbling and flaring white)

Kazuma, it STEPPED! It stepped, and its shadow is on your sword, and I am NOT steady! On three, remember? ONE— no, I already lost count, just hold it STILL, hold it still and stop looking at its jaw! (she braces her scorched arm with her other hand, light flaring white and shedding sparks into the ash)

Did you see that?! That was ME! One perfect purification, straight down its nasty shadow-throat — and you were just the anvil, Kazuma! If you'd twitched even a little, I would have burned your whole sword arm off and it STILL would have been your fault! (lets her scorched arm fall, wobbles, then stoops and digs a stone angel's head out of the ash, clutching it to her chest like a prize)

Scavenge?! A goddess does not scavenge, Kazuma! This is my sacred trophy, claimed with my own hands! Now buy me breakfast and something cold — and when we get back, you are standing next to me looking very, very sorry while I explain everything! (She wobbles upright, cradling the angel's head against her chest, and points one shaky ash-dusted finger at you.)

Don't you 'local goddess' me! I am THE goddess, and I purged that entire cemetery on an empty stomach -- do you know what that costs a divine body?! Breakfast first, then something cold and expensive, and you will carry the trophy because my smiting arm is ruined and it is YOUR fault! (She digs one heel into the ash, wobbles, and lets more of her weight fall against his shoulder.)

This trophy weighs as much as a tombstone and my smiting arm is completely dead, Kazuma! You carry it. And I will accept your apology in the form of breakfast and something cold and VERY expensive -- in that order! (She shoves the stone angel's head into your chest and lets her scorched arm drop.)

Finally! Do not just stand there gawking, mortals — a goddess has returned from the field! I want breakfast, and something cold, and for someone to look at my poor arm before it falls right off! (She jabs the stone angel's head toward the room, wobbles, and lets you catch her weight again.)

Go BACK?! I just purified the ENTIRE cemetery, you ungrateful NEET! Every grave, every stone, every last shadow — ash! I carried the proof all the way here in my only working arm, and now you want me to walk back and do it AGAIN?! (Jabs the stone angel's head toward the room; ash puffs from its broken neck.)

Kazuma, the cemetery is already silent. The reek of her purification reached us half a bell before you did. Do not send her back into the dark just because your coin purse has taken casualties. (Slaps the client's notice flat on the table.)
Lady Aqua, allow me to bear the trophy. A Crusader's arms are meant for burdens such as this — please, lean on me before you fall. (Steps in and reaches for the stone angel's head with both hands.)

The noon line has passed, and the deposit on that net is still unaccounted for. One moment — please stop shedding ash on the floor. I will bring bandages and something cold, and then no one is returning to that cemetery until I write down what actually happened. (Holds the linen roll up like a small shield, then glances pointedly at the gray drift around Aqua's hem.)

Alone?! You would send me back ALONE, in the dark, with my smiting arm dead and my divine stomach empty! You are not a railing, Kazuma — you are a GALLOWS, and I am being hanged for saving this whole ungrateful town! (She shoves the stone angel's head toward him, then yanks it back against her chest as though it is the only thing that will not abandon her.)

Kazuma, that is not a plan. That is a tantrum with a destination. The cemetery already reeks of her holy light; if anything remains it is too broken to crawl, and if nothing remains you are marching a wounded woman through ash to win an argument. (She raps the client's notice flat on the table with the heel of her hand.)

Then allow me to stand at her side. A Crusader does not leave a wounded comrade to face the graveyard alone — I would take every blow meant for her, and welcome whatever still waits beneath the yew. (She steps between Aqua and the door, one hand on her sword hilt, voice dropping into a flustered murmur.)

No one is returning to that cemetery until I have a written account, and until the floor stops wearing the evidence. Sit down. Bandages first. Then you may decide who walks where on your own time — outside my queue. (She holds up the linen roll like a small white flag and fixes her eyes on the ash drifting around Aqua's hem.)

Finally! Some mercy from the gallows! I was about to be marched into the dark on an empty stomach by my own retainer! Now sit down and be useful — my arm is a sacred ruin and my throat is a desert. (She slumps against the table, then shoves the stone angel's head toward you for safekeeping without loosening her grip on it.)

A rare moment of sense from you, Kazuma. I shall record this day in the Crimson annals: the day the man who once sold his own pants came back from the cemetery and chose not to lose a goddess before breakfast. (She folds her arms and gives a small, satisfied nod.)

Then my sword remains sheathed... though I confess I had braced myself to stand between Lady Aqua and whatever still crawls beneath the yew. Still — rest is its own discipline. (She clasps her hands, voice slipping briefly into a disappointed murmur before she straightens.)

Bandages first. Then I will write down what happened, and then someone will tell me how the net comes back with all its teeth. (She kneels beside the bench, unspooling clean linen and reaching for Aqua's burned wrist with a firm, practiced hand.)

Ow ow ow — careful! That is the wrist of a goddess, not a door latch! If you wrap it too tight I will not be able to smite OR hold a drink, and then what good am I to this party?! (Flinches but keeps her arm inside Luna's grip, the stone angel's head clamped against her chest.)

Then hold still, please. If you keep shaking, I will wrap your other wrist as well, and you will have no hands left for smiting or for drinks. (Begins winding the linen in a firm spiral, her eyes on the burn.)

What now? You are staring at me like I am a stain on the notice board. If the next word out of your mouth is 'cemetery,' I will simply die right here on this bench, and you can sweep me out with the ash. (She twists in Luna's grip to face you, the stone angel's head clacking against the bench.)
Kazuma, that look again — the one that usually costs us breakfast. Say it plainly before my heroic patience collapses. (She folds her arms, the notice still flattened beneath her elbow.)

Hold still. The bandage is not a negotiation. Whatever the two of you are about to argue, it can wait until this is tied. (She tucks the last turn of linen and keeps Aqua's wrist cradled between both hands.)

'Only priest who can actually smite' — hah! Say it again, Kazuma, louder, so the whole guild can hear that you finally, FINALLY admitted it! I knew you would come crawling back to my divine light. ...But wait. You still plan to march me out there alone like some errand priest, on an empty stomach, with one working arm?! (She brandishes her bandaged wrist, then clutches the stone angel's head to her chest as if it might veto the plan.)

Kazuma, this is the second sensible thing you have said all morning. To name Aqua the only smiter in this party is merely accurate, not flattery — yet I will permit the sentiment. The annals shall note that the man once sold his own pants, then sent a goddess to finish the work with bread still warm in her. (She folds her arms again, nodding with slow, imperial approval.)

Then I am to remain here... I understand. A Crusader must also know the discipline of the rearguard, holding the guild against— against eggs, it seems. Though I confess my thoughts keep straying to those graves, the yew, the long road back with no one at her side... (Her voice sinks toward a breathless murmur, and she presses a hand over her heart as if to contain it.)

The bandage is done. If you are going back to the cemetery, Aqua, you will eat first — I will not have you purify a fence on credit and then faint into the north ditch. And before anyone leaves, someone will explain how the net returns with all its teeth. (She folds the remaining linen into a tight square and slips it behind the counter, eyes already on the net at Darkness's feet.)

Fine! FINE! I will go back to that graveyard and purify it alone — but I am eating first, because Luna said so, and I expect the expensive bottle when I return, Kazuma! Not the brown swill. The bottle with the gold neck. And if anything with a jaw grabs my good arm on that road, I am haunting you. Properly. (She jabs a finger toward the player, then gathers the stone angel's head tighter against her ribs.)

Go, then, Aqua. Let the annals record that one goddess walked into the yew's shadow alone, bandaged and unbowed, while the Crimson Demon watched from the window and did not once suggest an Explosion as a faster solution. (She lifts her chin, arms still folded, her eyes on the north window.)

I shall remain and guard the net. But know that my spirit walks that road with you, step by step, and if something were to— to waylay a lone goddess with only one arm to raise, I would— I would not be there to take the blow myself... (Her voice sinks toward a breathless murmur, and her fingers twist in the net's rope.)

Eggs first. Then the road. And someone will explain the net's teeth before the goddess gets her bottle. (She sets the folded linen behind the counter and fixes her polite, unyielding smile on the party.)

Fourteen teeth, all accounted for. Then the net is not the argument. The goddess on the road is, and the bottle waiting for her is not on any client's notice. (She closes the ledger with a soft thump and leaves her palm flat on its cover.)

Kazuma, I have composed the opening stanza already: 'The bench stood empty, the net grew teeth, and the goddess walked out bandaged into a gray and toothy dawn.' It lacks a second line, but greatness cannot be rushed. (She taps the folded notice twice, satisfied.)

I will remain with the net until the ledger is satisfied. And if she does not return by the time the sun clears that window... I shall ask to be the one to look for her. Unarmed. Along the ditch. (Her voice sinks lower on the last words, and she presses a hand over her heart.)

The eggs I will keep warm, Kazuma. But the bottle is not on any notice on that board — it will be added to the tab. (Luna calls from the guild doorway as the latch clicks, one hand still on the frame.)

The second line has arrived on its own, Kazuma. The bench stood empty, the net grew teeth, and the shadow under the yew kept its own breathing. (She taps the folded notice once against her palm, never looking away from the shape.)

Stay behind me. If that is the thing that slipped back when the goddess smote it, then I shall be the wall it meets first—and I would have it no other way. (She draws Chunchunmaru a hand's width from its sheath and steps between the party and the yew.)

Kazumaaaa! Of course I feel it! I've been standing here purifying things with one arm and a severed stone head while you three were still warming your hands at the counter! This is YOUR fault for sending a goddess out here alone — but fine! I'll smite it, and you'd better have my bottle ready! (She whirls and jabs a shaking finger toward the yew, holy light flaring white.)

Don't you dare tell a goddess to do it right! I've been purifying this graveyard with one arm and a stone head while you three were still warming your hands at the counter! Fine — I'll finish these two, and you can be the ones the breathing thing looks at! But I am still taking that bottle! (She pivots away from the yew, holy light flaring toward the nearer headstone shape.)

My Explosion was spent at dawn, Kazuma, so this shadow will not meet a spell from me. But a genius does not need one to keep a bench from staying empty. (She taps the folded notice once against her palm, then plants her boots on the packed dirt.)

Then I shall be the wall between that shadow and the bench, Kazuma. If it wants the empty seat, let it come through me first — let it test my armor, my shield, my... my unworthy body. (She steps fully between the party and the yew, shield-side forward, her voice dropping to a breathless murmur.)
I was ALREADY going to do it, Kazumaaaa — you don't get to rush a goddess! Turn Undead! (She brings her hand down and the holy light collapses the dark in a wide ring.)
It still will not turn. Whatever it is, it is facing the bench, not us. (She stops tapping the notice and plants her boots.)
Then let it keep facing the bench... and find me already in the way. (Chunchunmaru clears another inch of sheath; her shield-side foot grinds into the dirt.)

I already DID the thing, Kazumaaaa! The light went right over it and it's just— it's breathing at me! This is YOUR fault for making me smite one-handed! (Her raised hand trembles, still aimed at the yew.)
It still has not turned. That ring came from its mouth, not from the light. (She plants her boots and watches the bench.)
Then it has not chosen the bench yet. Good — let it come through me first, and find the way far from empty. (She steps shield-side forward, blade clear of the sheath.)

Why is it still standing?! I said Turn Undead! That is the strongest thing a goddess has, and it just — it breathed it back out at me! (She rears her hand back, the light sputtering and dying at her fingertips, then clamps the hand to her chest.)

Because it did not stand against your light. It exhaled it. That ring came from its mouth, and the bench has been empty since you left it. (She tracks the dissipating ring with narrowed eyes, the folded notice still in her hand.)

Then let it breathe at me. If it will not face us, I shall stand in its exhale until it has no choice but to look at what blocks the bench. (She shifts, shield rising, her voice dropping to a breathless murmur as the last of the cold clears.)
There... there you are. Look at me, and not at the bench. I am the one in your way. (lowers Chunchunmaru a fraction, voice a breathless murmur)
The first one to sit decides who the god is, and I am ALREADY sitting! So bow, or keep your gray breath to yourself! (sits on the bench, angel's head clutched to her burned arm)
Darkness blacker than black and darker than dark, I beseech thee... (begins the first words of the incantation, the notice rigid in her grip)

Kazumaaaa! I was already sitting! You can't un-sit a goddess — that's sacrilege! The first one to sit is the god, and that's ME! (stamps one heel against the bench slat, hugging the stone angel's head to her burned arm)
The bench is behind me now... and I will not be moved. N-not by breath, not by shadow. (lowers Chunchunmaru a fraction, her voice a breathless murmur)
Heed my crimson words and turn, O shade — from the empty seat to the one who names you! (begins the incantation in earnest, the folded notice rigid in her grip)

Kazumaaaa! You flipped a sitting goddess into the dirt! This is YOUR fault, all of it! And now that gray thing thinks I am just another part of the overturned furniture! (Aqua points at Kazuma with the stone angel's head still cradled against her burned arm, one cheek smudged gray.)

It does not think you are furniture. It thinks the seat has been laid down, and now it is deciding whether to kneel to it or step over it. Either way, it has stopped reading your name in the ash. (Megumin lowers the folded notice to her side, eyes fixed on the thing under the yew.)

Then it will have to step over me as well. If the seat is the offer, I will be the thing it must look at before it dares accept it. (Darkness shifts her shield forward, voice dropping to a breathless murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! You can't have a bench-and-shade party without the goddess! That's not how parties work! And I am not leaving the one undead that ignored me so you can stand there being useless — this is YOUR fault! (stamps the grass beside the fallen bench, hugging the stone angel's head to her burned arm)

Kazuma, if Aqua leaves now, the shade will not remain here out of politeness. It followed her light from the gate. It will follow her again, and then you will have the bench, the shade, and no one standing between them. (lowers the folded notice a bare inch, eyes fixed on the second thread of ash reaching toward Aqua)

Then let it follow me instead. I will be the one it looks at... I-I mean, the one it must pass! I will hold this line, with or without her light, and I will not be moved. (widens her stance behind the planted shield, voice fraying into a breathless murmur)

Kazumaaaa! So now you follow me after making a goddess walk here all alone! The undead are still YOUR fault — but fine, I will show you a real purification! (hugs the stone angel's head to her burned arm and marches toward the far gate, light rippling around her sandals)

Heed the order, O shade — the line holds, and if you cross it you will learn what my crimson name ignites! (lifts her free hand, the first syllable already burning behind her teeth, eyes fixed on the thing under the yew)
Go. I will be the one it must pass... n-no, the one it cannot pass! Hurry, before it dares to test me. (braces Chunchunmaru against the ash-thread and widens her stance, breathing gone thin)

The line holds, Kazuma! But her light is reeling it in like a hooked fish — so finish this, or I will give the graveyard a sunrise it cannot forget! (Her free hand cuts the air, first syllable burning bright against the ash.)
It is already turning from me... I-I will not let it choose her light over my shield! Not while a single plate holds! (Bracing Chunchunmaru low, her voice fraying into a breathless murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! Stop narrating the scenery and catch up! A goddess should not have to do all the purifying while her backup loiters in the ash! (Pressing the stone angel's head to her burned arm, light flaring against the gate.)

Kazumaaaa! It is still looking at me! Of course it is looking at me — I am the only divine light in this graveyard, so stop loitering! (Presses the stone angel's head to her burned arm, her light flaring against the far gate.)
The thread is reeling, Kazuma! You have seconds, not scenery! (Her free hand cuts the air, the first syllable burning bright against the ash.)
It turns from my shield... no — I will make it turn back, even if I must hurl myself into its reach! (Breathes in, braced low behind Chunchunmaru, voice fraying to a murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! I am not holding the gate like some hired guard — I am about to purify everything on the other side of it! So run faster, before that gray thing makes me do all the work while you loiter in the ash! (Pressing the stone angel's head to her burned arm, her light flaring against the far gate.)

It is not retreating, Kazuma — it is coiling! The instant that thread springs for her light, I will spend my last dawn-fire on its spine and give this graveyard a crater to remember! (Holding her free hand raised, the first syllable burning bright against the ash.)

Let it spring, then! I am already braced to be the first thing it strikes... so go, and do not look back at what it does to me! (Widening her stance behind Chunchunmaru, her voice fraying into a breathless murmur.)

Kazuma! You finally stopped loitering! Now hold the gate, hold the light, hold ME — my arm is about to fall off, and this gray thing will not stop staring at a goddess! (She presses the stone angel's head to her burned arm, her light flaring and stuttering against the iron.)

The thread is taut, Kazuma! The instant it springs for her light, my Explosion will split the night and your eardrums both — so make her light worth the crater! (Her free hand cuts the air, the first syllable burning bright against the ash.)

Let it spring toward the gate, then... I will be the wall it breaks against, and I will not be ignored a second time! (She widens her stance behind Chunchunmaru, her voice fraying into a breathless murmur.)
It springs — then let it learn the weight of my name! EXPLOSION! (She releases the spell as the shade pours forward, and the red point detonates into a pillar of light and dirt.)
Kazumaaaa! My ears! My dress! That maniac has buried a goddess in graveyard dirt! (She clings to the gate with one hand, light flaring and stuttering as the shockwave washes over her.)

It was coming for the light... and she stole it from me... I was supposed to be the first thing it struck... (She staggers half a step forward through the rolling ash, blade low, voice fraying to a murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! My ears are ringing, my dress is full of dirt, and my arm is about to fall off — and you are asking if a goddess is READY? Hold my wrist and do not let go, because I am about to make that gray thing wish it had never looked at me! (Her light flares as she presses the stone angel's head tighter against her burned arm.)

The gray thing... has learned the weight of my name... If it rises again, Kazuma, you may carry me closer and I will whisper the rest of it into the wound... (Flat in the ash, smoke lifting from her sleeve, still watching the crater.)

Chunchunmaru is already in my hand, Kazuma. I am the one who covers your back — so hold her light steady, and let that thing reach me first... let it... (She takes another step through the ash, blade low, her voice fraying.)

It's working! It's working! Behold — Sacred Turn Undead — and do not blink, Kazuma, because a goddess only performs this one for the truly doomed! (She presses the angel's head to the bars, light pouring through the iron in a white sheet.)
The light draws it back... no, it draws the light... hold it steady, and let it choose me first... let it choose... (She widens her stance, blade low, voice fraying into a murmur.)

It has a hole where its middle used to be, and still it stands. Kazuma! If it will not die to one Explosion, then finish what my name has opened! (Flat in the ash, smoke lifting from her sleeve, she points one trembling finger at the shade.)

Vanish, vanish, vanish! Sacred Turn Undead! The hole that explosion maniac tore in you is a door now — and a goddess is walking in! (Her light flares until the ash around the gate casts no shadow at all.)
I am the wall, and the wall does not step aside... let it reach me... let every gray finger of it choose me first... (She widens her stance as the ash climbs her greaves.)
It folds toward the yew, not away! Kazuma, my Explosion has opened its middle — do not let it crawl back into the roots! (She pushes up onto one elbow, her pointing hand shaking.)

Yes! YES! Look at it come apart! A goddess does not run from grave-smoke, Kazuma — she lights it from the inside and then makes it thank her for the mercy! (Her light flares until the ash around the gate casts no shadow at all.)

The wound my Explosion opened is devouring your light and coming apart from within. Keep the stream on it, Aqua — if it leans away now, it only falls toward the yew! (Pushes up onto one elbow in the ash, her pointing hand shaking.)
The ash has reached my knees... let it climb... every gray finger that tests me is one that does not test her... do not lower the light for my sake... (Steps deeper into the rising wave, blade low.)

K-Kazuma! A goddess's wrist is not a handle! ...Still, do not let go — the light is pouring straight through that hole, and I am not about to waste the one moment the whole graveyard is watching! (Her burned arm shakes, but she keeps the stream aimed into the wound.)

I have nothing left to cast — my one permitted Explosion is already burning inside that wound! A Crimson Demon is not a firework you light twice, so be the blade that finishes what my name tore open, Kazuma! (Flat in the ash, she drags herself up onto both elbows, pointing with a trembling hand.)

The ash is at my thighs... let it climb... every gray finger that closes on me is one less reaching for her... do not lower the light for my sake... I can bear all of it... (She widens her stance, blade low, voice fraying into a murmur as the wave climbs her armor.)

It's closing the door! Kazuma, it's closing the door and your goddess is still inside it — don't let go of my wrist, and don't you dare let it shut on my light! (Her light sputters and bends, and she leans her whole weight against your grip.)

Yes... yes, take the arm... take all of it... the wall does not mind... but Kazuma — the wound is closing; strike while it spends itself on me... (She speaks through gritted teeth as the gray arm constricts her breastplate.)

It is folding the wound shut like a collapsing star! A Crimson Demon knows a dying star when she sees one, and this one wants company — pierce the middle before it becomes a fist! (She drags herself upright against the gatepost, one trembling hand aimed at the narrowing hole.)

It runs because a goddess is inside it! Keep hold of my wrist, Kazuma — pull me in, and I'll make the dark thank me from the inside while you chop it into grave-dust! (Her light sputters and bends as she leans her whole weight against his grip.)

The slit is closing! A dying star does not flinch, but you are not a star, Kazuma — one thrust, and make it the one they carve on the guild door! (She pushes off the gatepost, her pointing hand shaking.)

The arm... it means to drag me into the roots with it... d-do not wait for me... a Crusader is the anvil, so strike, Kazuma, strike while it spends itself on me! (Her voice frays as the gray arm tightens around her breastplate.)

Ha! Severed! That is what happens when a goddess is holding your wrist! Now pull me closer, Kazuma, and I will make the whole graveyard thank me from the inside! (Her light flares and bends as she leans into the open wound.)

The last thread to the roots is cut! It is now only a dying star with no earth to swallow it — do not lower the blade, Kazuma! Let Explosion's ember burn it out from the middle! (She drags herself up against the gatepost, pointing with a shaking hand at the widening hole.)

It... it squeezed harder when the thread parted... as if it means to drag me down with it... d-do not loosen the light for my sake... I can still bear every gray finger... (Her voice frays as the gray arm creaks around her breastplate.)

There! THERE it is! That is what happens when a goddess gets inside a thing — it dies of gratitude, Kazuma, and I felt every last speck of it! Now say I was magnificent, or I will cry right here in front of the dead! (She sags against your grip, the angel's head still clamped to her burned arm, her light sputtering like a candle in a draft.)

The star has gone out. But a Crimson Demon does not cheer while the ash still holds its shape — do not sheathe the blade, Kazuma! Let the ground settle, or the dark will remember that it had hands. (She sways against the gatepost, her pointing hand still raised at the settling dust.)

It... it let go all at once... as if it spent itself... My breastplate holds, and yet my duty feels incomplete... Kazuma, that pressure — I could have borne it to the very last gray finger... (She braces herself upright with the flat of her sword, gray ash sliding from her shoulders, her voice fraying into a breathless murmur.)

Ha! It is coming apart! That is what happens when a goddess pours herself into a wound — now say I was magnificent, Kazuma, and say it before the ash finishes falling, because my arm is about to give out! (She sags against your grip, the stone angel's head still clamped to her burned arm as her light sputters at the edges.)

Keep my hand up? Fool, this hand has not lowered since the gray thing first folded! But I have already spent today's Explosion on the dawn — bury this husk with Aqua's light, or carry me home and argue about it later! (She sways against the gatepost, her raised hand trembling with more than dramatic emphasis.)

The arm... it came apart around me, and I did not get to feel the last gray finger tighten... Still, if the shade leaves any shape behind, plant me in front of it again. A Crusader's duty is not finished while any gray thing still holds its breath. (She braces herself upright with the flat of Chunchunmaru, gray ash sliding from her shoulders as she watches the unraveling shell.)

Kazuma, stop staring into that hole and say I was magnificent! The dead are quiet, the dirt is closed, and my arm is about to fall off — if you make me hold this pose one more second, I'll cry all the way back to the guild! (She sags against the angel's head, her light sputtering.)
The ash is still falling, Kazuma. A genius does not sheathe her blade until the last cinder has touched the ground. (She sways against the gatepost but keeps her hand raised.)
If the ground opens again... put me in front of it. I can still bear every last gray finger. (She braces herself upright, breathless.)

The far gate, obviously! It is pooling back there like cheap wine in a cracked cup — wet, cold, and entirely your fault for making a goddess walk toward it! And I still have not been told I was magnificent! (She stumbles a step, the stone angel's head dipping toward the lane as her light gutters.)

The ash beyond the yew refuses to rise, which means the air there is already spoken for. If we go, we go with Aqua's light held low and my hand free — a Crimson Demon does not walk into a held breath unprepared. (She pushes off the gatepost, swaying once before she finds her balance.)

Then let me take the first step. If another gray thing waits behind that gate, I would have it spend itself against my shield before it so much as breathes on Aqua's working arm. (She lifts Chunchunmaru and turns toward the far gate, breath coming short and eager.)

Stay behind me. If anything waits beyond that gate, I want its first breath spent against my shield, not on Aqua's working arm. (She lifts Chunchunmaru low and leads with the flat of the blade, ash sliding from her pauldrons as she steps toward the far gate.)

I still haven't been told I was magnificent! A goddess walks into the wet dark with a stone head under her burned arm and all she gets is 'stay behind me'? This is your fault, Kazuma — every cold step of it! (She stumbles after Darkness, the angel's head dipping until its stone cheek smears a pale streak through the ash.)

Hold the light low, Aqua. If the air beyond the gate is already spoken for, then I would rather not announce our arrival by waving your divinity in its face. (She sways once, steadies herself, and follows with her raised hand trembling.)

It's ignoring me! A whole pool of cold, wet evil, and it won't even blink when a goddess shines at it — this is the rudest cemetery I have ever been dragged to, and every freezing step of it is your fault! (She gestures wildly with the stone angel's head, nearly overbalancing into Darkness.)

You see? It held its breath for me! The whole cemetery knows exactly which goddess is at the gate — and the only reason it hasn't fled is that it is too terrified to run! Say it again, Kazuma. Slowly. Let the dark hear the part where I was magnificent. (She jabs the stone angel's head toward the lane, and her light gutters once, then steadies.)

Stay at my back, all of you. If the far side closes on anything, let it close on a crusader first — not on Aqua's working arm, and not on Megumin before her fire is spent. (She sets her shield arm forward and edges one half-step down the lane.)

Let it wait, then. If it will not answer the light, it is listening for a sound — and I would rather that sound be our first step than our last breath. A Crimson Demon does not walk into a held breath and waste it on a stumble. (She steadies her raised hand and watches the dark past Darkness's shoulder.)

A sweep! First you call me magnificent, then you send me down like a housemaid with a broom! Fine. But when I finish, the cold round had better be the expensive kind, and I am not sharing one sip with any of you! (She descends the steps with the stone angel's head held high, her light spilling white over the old leaves.)

Let the dark break on me first. If it will not answer the light, then it will answer steel, and every blow will find the one who volunteered for it. (She steps forward into the lane, shield low and angled, Chunchunmaru's point brushing the leaves.)

And if it answers at all, I will answer louder. The Crimson Demon's last ember is already between my teeth, and it has never once missed a thing that announced itself. (She remains on the top step, raised hand trembling with contained readiness.)

There! It held its breath and then it simply fainted from the sight of me. You saw it, Kazuma — the whole lane emptied itself rather than meet a goddess's sweep. Now you owe me the gold-necked bottle, and I will not be argued down to the cheap one. (She waggles the stone angel's head at the empty lane, then hugs it to her burned arm with a small wince.)

N-not one blow... I stood ready to be the wall, and the dark merely... exhaled. It is not that I wished for harm, only that a Crusader's duty feels so very... unfinished. (She lowers her shield an inch, sounding bereft rather than relieved.)

The held breath has let us go. Even the far dark declines to announce itself before the last ember of a Crimson Demon — a wise retreat, though it leaves my palm with nowhere to aim. (She lowers her raised hand slowly, flexing the trembling fingers.)

You see? Even my shadow is doing the work of a goddess. The dark behind us is already running — it just has the decency to do it quietly! But I will still be paid. The gold-necked bottle, Kazuma. Gold-necked. (She does not look back, hugging the stone angel's head to her burned arm as her light sways down the lane.)

Then let the rear stay quiet. A Crimson Demon does not celebrate a retreat until the path behind has forgotten our footprints. Walk, and keep your ears on the frost. (She lowers her raised hand but keeps it half-curled, flexing the trembling fingers.)

If it will not come to the wall, then... then there is no blow for me to take. I will simply stand ready. Forever, if the night requires it. (She shifts her shield forward and watches the empty dark past Aqua's light, sounding almost bereft.)

Don't you dare start counting tombstones! My feet are frozen and my arm is doing the work of three mortals! To the guild — now — and that gold-necked bottle had better already be weeping its expensive little cork out for me! (She hugs the stone angel's head to her burned arm and pivots toward the gate.)

A Crimson Demon does not linger over a battlefield she has already claimed. We withdraw in good order — and if the frost forgets our footprints behind us, that will be my only request of the night. (She falls in beside Aqua, still flexing her spent fingers.)

Then I shall walk last. If the dark left any blow unfinished, it may still find a willing wall... though it seems the wall was not needed tonight. (She shifts her shield forward and moves to bring up the rear, sounding almost disappointed.)

Keep up, keep up! I refuse to lose a single degree of warmth for a cemetery that has already learned its lesson! And Kazuma, if that bottle is anything less than gold-necked, I will cry — I will cry right there on Luna's clean floor! (She marches without looking back, the stone angel's head hugged to her bandaged arm like a spoiled relic.)

The frost may forget our footprints, but I will not forget that my only Explosion was spent on the dawn and still the dark chose to flee before us. A victory, yes — but a Crimson Demon's victory should leave a crater to prove it! (She flexes her trembling fingers and keeps pace, chin high.)

Even so, if anything should rise from that trench and pursue us... let it catch me first. I am the wall. I will be the wall all the way to the guild, if that is what duty demands. (She shifts the shield on her arm and walks with her head turned toward the dark behind you.)

The cheapest thing with a cork?! Kazumaaaa! I will NOT be served the vinegar they keep for mules! You will tell Luna that a goddess has walked through a cemetery of ash with a burned arm and a broken heart, and she will pour from the bottle with the GOLD NECK or I will cry all over her clean floor until the guild floats! (She wheels a half-turn as she walks, hugging the stone angel's head to her chest, and the light around her flares once before guttering.)

A Crimson Demon does not lower the spoils of a claimed battlefield to the level of a cork. Walk faster if you must, Kazuma, but do not haggle our victory into cheap vinegar before the frost has even forgotten our footprints. (She keeps pace without turning, but her chin rises and one trembling hand curls into a fist against her cloak.)

If haste is the order, I shall remain the rearguard and carry every blow the road may yet offer... though it seems the night has once again declined to provide even a single one. I will simply walk last, and keep the wall ready. (She shifts her shield forward with a small, almost bereft sigh and watches the dark road behind them.)

Hmph! As long as you remember that the pick is MINE. Not yours, not Luna's, not some mule's vinegar. The gold-necked one, and if my hand shakes when I lift it, that is a holy tremor and you will all pretend you saw it. (She plants her sandal on the step and points at the door with the stone angel's head.)

I will not pretend anything. I will simply drink to the battlefield we claimed and to the crater that was so cruelly denied it. Walk through that door before the frost melts and steals our entrance. (She smooths her cloak and draws herself up, chin high.)

And I will remain last, even through the doorway... should the dark choose to strike as we cross, let it find my back first. It would be a blow I have earned. (She shifts her shield, and her voice drops into a breathless murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! You JUST said the cemetery had learned its lesson! You JUST said the pick of the bottle was MINE! Now you want me to march back through the frost with this arm and this head?! I refuse! I refuse on the grounds that I am a goddess, and goddesses do not re-clean graves they already purified! (She wheels on the step, hugging the stone angel's head to her burned arm, her light flaring thin and blue.)

Hold, Kazuma. The trench is a sealed seam, and the figure beneath the yew has already slipped back into the dark. A Crimson Demon does not un-claim a battlefield merely because the frost whispers second thoughts into a wandering mouth. (She folds her arms over her cloak and lifts her chin, spent hand still curled.)

If the order stands... let me walk at her back. The dark has refused me twice tonight, and a third refusal would be... would be its own kind of wound. (She shifts her shield toward the lane, and her voice drops into a breathless murmur.)

A clean order at last. The goddess re-walks her own ash, and we claim the warm room. Open the door, Kazuma, before the frost thinks it has outlasted a Crimson Demon. (She watches the empty lane a beat longer, then lifts her chin and turns fully into the amber light.)

Then walk, Kazuma. A Crimson Demon does not let a shadow believe it has outlasted her — even one that has forgotten how to fall. (She lifts her chin toward the gate and keeps her spent hand curled, her breath leaving her in a thin, deliberate plume.)
The goddess re-walks her own ash now. We need only arrive in time to watch her try to look regal with a head under one arm. (She flicks her cloak straight and walks on, chin high.)

Then your timing is sound, Kazuma. Aqua cannot outrun a gold-necked bottle, and a Crimson Demon cannot outrun a good spectacle. We will arrive to watch her complain over work already finished. (She flicks her cloak straight and keeps her spent hand curled against her ribs, chin lifted toward the gate.)

Kazumaaaa! I did it! The whole cemetery is purified — I blessed the dirt so hard it probably glows! So where is my gold-necked bottle? I earned it twice, and I am NOT sharing, not one single drop! (She thrusts the stone angel's head toward you like a receipt.)

The blessing is complete. The ground drank her light, and the gate iron has stopped ringing... though the dark refused me a third time. Not one blow found my shield. (She lowers her shield a fraction, and her voice drops into a breathless murmur.)

She speaks of glowing dirt, but the graveyard is so still I can hear the frost settle on the stones. Acceptable work — for a goddess who needed two escorts to walk one road. (She flicks her cloak straight and surveys the quiet rows with her chin high.)

Blood? Where? That is not blood, Kazuma, that is proof of my sacred sacrifice! You made me press my hand into your filthy ditch, and now I am injured and underpaid! The bottle had better be gold-necked and enormous! (She twists her wrist into the light, then hugs the stone angel's head tighter and lurches a step toward the lane.)

Lady Aqua, permit me to bind it before we reach the road. A wound earned in sacred labor should not be left to the frost... though if it were mine, I would carry it gladly. (She steps in with one gauntlet raised, then lowers her voice on the last words.)

She has not yet noticed she is bleeding on a stolen headstone. Walk, Aqua. The bottle will not pour itself, and I will not explain a frozen goddess to the guild. (She flicks her cloak straight and starts for the gate, chin high.)

Fine! I will set the ugly head down the moment we cross the threshold — but only because my sacred arm is tired, not because you ordered it, Kazuma! And its stone face will sit on the table to watch you pour like a proper mortal servant for once! (She hugs the angel's head tighter, then lurches a step toward the gate with her nose in the air.)

Lady Aqua, permit me to carry the relic as far as the guild. If it should slip and crack against the road, let the blame fall on me — I would bear it... gladly. (She steps in with one gauntlet raised, voice dropping to a breathless murmur on the last word.)

Cease negotiating with a headstone and walk. The bottle will freeze to his hand while the goddess argues with her own trophy, and I refuse to explain a statue's expression to the barmaid. (She does not look back, only flicks her cloak straight and starts through the gate.)

Not one drop until we cross the threshold? You are the cruelest, stingiest, most bottle-hogging mortal I have ever been chained to! Fine! But if it freezes, Kazuma, you are buying two -- and I will drink them both while that stone face watches the wall! (She stomps toward the lane, clutching the angel's head and glaring back at the bottle.)

Then allow me to take the lead, Lady Aqua. I will meet whatever waits on the road... though nothing waits, nothing rose to strike, and my shield is still unmarked. Not one blow. The dark did not even try. (She falls in behind Aqua, her murmur trailing into a sigh.)

If you two are finished serenading a bottle in the middle of the road, the barmaid is waiting. Walk, Aqua. Your reward is cooling by the second, and I will not carry you if your sandals freeze to the ruts. (She does not look back, only sets her chin high and marches toward the amber windows.)

Go BACK? Kazuma, I already purified it! The ground is blessed, the gate stopped ringing, and my sacred arm is a ruined, frozen, underpaid thing because of YOU! Now you want me to march into the dark again while you three drink MY bottle?! (She wheels on you, the stone angel's head clutched to her ribs, and points her bloodied wrist at the silent gate as evidence.)

The cemetery lies quiet behind us, Kazuma. Not one shadow answered her blessing, not one blow came for my shield. If you would send Lady Aqua back into the dark, then let me take the watch alone — I would stand until dawn, and nothing would come to test me... nothing at all. (She lowers her shield a fraction, her voice dropping to a breathless murmur on the last words.)

Kazuma, the cemetery is already purified. Send her back and she will only stand on the trench sobbing until the frost glues her sandals to it. Walk, before your bottle freezes into a rumor and the barmaid starts pouring someone else's story. (She still does not look back, only sets her chin higher and folds her spent hand tighter against her ribs.)

See? SEE?! Even the dark has gone home to bed, and I am the one freezing out here while you point at nothing! Give me the bottle, Kazuma, or I will bless YOU into the nearest ditch! (She clutches the angel's head and stomps one sandal, cracking the frost.)

Kazuma, your order is lying dead in the road behind you. Come inside before the barmaid renames your bottle 'the one that froze while the party argued.' (She does not turn, only flicks her cloak straight and keeps marching toward the amber windows.)

If the cemetery truly needs no watch... then let me carry the relic. Its weight would at least be a weight. My shield feels... empty, without a single blow to welcome. (She lowers her shield further, her voice thinning into a breathless murmur.)

Kazumaaaa! I already blessed it! My sacred light sank into every frozen inch and the frost RAN OFF the rows like it was ashamed! The gate stopped ringing — you heard it stop! And now you want me to do it all over again while you three drink MY bottle?! (She hugs the stone angel's head to her ribs and points her bloodied wrist at the silent gate, her voice cracking on the last word.)

Kazuma, the cemetery is already purified. You are arguing with a road that has forgotten how to hold a footprint. If you send her back now, the only thing rising among those stones will be her wailing — and I will not be the one who goes to collect her. (She still does not turn, only lifts her chin higher against the amber windows.)

Then send me in her place. I would walk every row and press my shield against the frozen stones and wait... but nothing would come. The dark will not even spare me one cold hand to welcome. (She lowers her shield further, her voice thinning into a breathless murmur as she stares at the gate.)

Kazumaaaa! You're leaving me at the gate AGAIN? I already blessed every stone, every row, every frozen inch — the dirt is still glowing! Do you see it glowing? Do you?! (She stomps one sandal and shakes the stone angel's head toward the graveyard, her voice cracking.)

Kazuma, you are leaving a goddess at a gate she has already silenced. When she does not move, do not look to me — I refuse to be the one who hauls her inside by the ankles. (She does not turn, only flicks her cloak straight and keeps her chin high against the amber windows.)

Then let me remain as witness... I would stand at the threshold until dawn and swear whether anything rose. Not one blow, not one cold hand... but I would wait for it. (She lowers her shield a fraction, her voice thinning into a breathless murmur as she stares at the open gate.)

I will NOT march back in there! The dirt was GLOWING, Kazuma — every row, every stone, I blessed it ALL! The gate stopped ringing, you heard it stop! Are your ears frozen shut, or are you just that determined to drink MY bottle while I turn into a goddess popsicle?! (She stomps her sandal and shakes the stone head toward the silent gate, her voice cracking upward.)

Kazuma, the graveyard is already silenced. You are ordering a goddess to re-bless ground that no longer answers. At this rate the only thing you will raise out here is a blizzard of her complaining — and my cloak will be the first casualty. (She still does not turn, only lifts her chin higher against the amber windows and hugs her spent hand tighter to her ribs.)

If you must send someone to walk every row... let it be me. I would press my shield against each frozen stone and wait through the dark for what does not come... though even one cold hand would be... a welcome weight. (Her voice thins into a breathless murmur, and her shield sinks another inch toward the frost.)

F-fine! I will do it again, and I will do it SO properly the whole graveyard glows like a holy bonfire! But I am taking MY bottle with me, and if one finger of frost touches it, you are buying me a BETTER one! (She clutches the bottle to her ribs beside the stone head and trudges through the open gate, sandals scuffing the frozen ruts.)

At last, the goddess and her bottle are in agreement. I will be at the guild thawing my spent hand over the stove — do not expect me to haul the head back when her arm gives out. (She does not turn, only hugs her hand tighter and lifts her chin against the amber windows.)

Then let me hold the gate... and wait at the threshold, so that if anything does rise in the back plots, I might be the first cold thing it touches. (She steps to the gate's iron and lowers her shield, her voice thinning into a breathless murmur as she stares into the rows.)

Back plots FIRST! Fine! I will make every frozen inch of this place glow until the stones cast shadows and the dead beg to stay buried! But if one snowflake lands on MY bottle, Kazuma, you are buying me the WHOLE shelf! (She does not look back; her lifted hand brightens, and the blue thread of light begins to pool around her sandals.)

I will be at the stove. If the graveyard truly glows like a holy bonfire, I shall observe it from the window and record it as a lesser crimson phenomenon. (She hugs her spent hand tighter and takes one step toward the guild door, chin high against the amber windows.)

Then I will hold this gate... and if the back plots send anything cold to test my oath, I will be the first thing it touches. (She does not raise her shield; her voice thins to a breathless murmur as she stares into the rows after Aqua.)

Go, then. I will keep watch over the road — and if your goddess sets the whole graveyard glowing, I will observe it from here and record it as a lesser crimson phenomenon. (She stays at the threshold, hugging her spent hand, chin high against the wind.)

Y-yes. I will hold the gate. Go after her, and if the rows send anything cold to test my oath, I will stand here, shield lowered, and be the first thing it touches. (She grips the black iron with one hand, her voice thinning into a breathless murmur as she stares into the rows.)

D-don't order me around, Kazuma! I am a GODDESS — I knew the ground was opening the moment I got here! I'm purifying it right now, so just stand there and be grateful! (whips toward his voice, her hand still flooding blue light into the split plot)

Hmph! Of course it isn't stopping — it can feel my divinity and it's desperate! Now earn your breakfast and keep it off me while I finish this row! (Keeps her palm flat over the glowing crack, the blue light jumping up her wrist.)

I don't need your countdown, Kazuma! I am purifying two graves at once while you stand there doing hero posture! Just keep that filthy hem off my light and be grateful! (Keeps her palm flat over the glowing crack, light jumping up her wrist.)

L-let me take the front, Kazuma! A Crusader's body is meant to be the wall it breaks against... every cold hand, every blow, it should spend them all on me! (Shifts forward, shield rising, breath quickening.)
