That shade has no footsteps, Kazuma — it does not walk, it pours. Do not let its hem touch you; even my crimson eyes cannot see what it drinks. (Plants her boots at your shoulder, spent hand pressed to her chest.)

Stay behind me — no, let it come to ME! Every inch of that cold hand should fall on a Crusader, not on her light! (Steps between Kazuma and the shade, shield raised, voice fraying into a breathless rush.)

It turns with her, Kazuma! It does not chase footprints — it chases the glow! The next plot is already giving up its frost! (Plants her staff, pointing at the blackening seam with her spent hand still curled at her chest.)

TWO at once, and you said a whole shelf! Now be a useful wall, Kazuma — I'm going to make every last row GLOW, and you can start paying for breakfast! (Stumbles toward the next split plot, hugging the stone angel's head, blue light already spilling down her arms again.)

I am not 'something nastier down there,' Kazuma! I'm the one making this whole frozen yard GLOW — so keep that filthy rag off my light and stop budgeting my breakfast! (Stumbles into the next split plot, hugging the stone angel's head, blue light already spilling down her arms.)

K-Kazuma... you would name me the wall yourself... Then I will take every inch of it — let the cold spend its whole strength against my shield! (Shifts forward another half step, shield low, breath quickening into short white flags.)

I am saving it, Kazuma — one Explosion, already promised to the dawn, and the grave will not get a second. But if that shade so much as turns its jaw toward her, my empty hand is already on the true name. (Plants her staff, spent hand pressed flat against her chest, watching the black seam run toward Aqua's light.)

Just keep it there one more second, Kazuma! The next plot is already glowing, and I am NOT stopping to scrape you off the stones before breakfast! (Stumbles to the far side of the split plot, both hands flooding blue light into the seam.)

At your feet... K-Kazuma, you would spend an Explosion at your own feet with me already between the flame and the grave... then I will not move one inch from between them! (Plants her shield beside you, breath coming short and white, body braced toward the shade.)

That is a destruction art, Kazuma, not a pebble toss — if I speak the true name at your feet, the gate, the wall, and every one of us will learn it together. But if the hem passes you, my hand is already on the name. (Watches the black seam run toward your shadow, spent hand pressed flat to her chest.)

Stop SHOVING me, Kazuma! I was already going! And when every frozen inch of this yard is GLOWING, you are buying me the whole shelf — not just breakfast! (Stumbles clear of the split plot, hugging the stone angel's head, blue light spilling down her arms as she regains her footing.)

You sent the light it follows walking away from us, Kazuma! The shade does not chase footprints — it chases the glow — and now it will pour through the gap you left me to hold! (Steps to bracket Kazuma, staff-butt grinding into the seam, spent hand still pressed flat to her chest.)

Then let it! Plant me in that gap, Kazuma — let the cold spend its whole strength on my shield while she carries that light to the far wall! (Slam her shield down across the shade's path, body braced behind it, breath coming in short white flags.)

Then the line is drawn here, Kazuma — the Crimson Demon's empty hand and the wall's steel between the shade and the light it would swallow. If it means to reach her, it must first learn what a door refuses. (Plants her staff against the seam, spent hand still pressed flat to her chest, chin high.)

Let it come, then... every inch of its cold against my shield. I will not yield one step, Kazuma — not when the whole strength of the grave has finally chosen to spend itself on me! (Slams her shield down a second time, breath coming in short white flags, body braced behind the rim.)

Kazuma, the shade is not waiting for you to finish weighing it. It has already chosen the glow — so choose as well, or stand aside and let the line be a line. (Grips the staff with both hands, chin high, eyes on the black smear running past Kazuma's boots.)

If you mean to go after her, then go! I will not move one inch — let it spend its whole strength on my shield while you follow that light! (Bares her teeth behind the shield rim, breath short and white, thighs braced.)

Then run, Kazuma! The name is already coiled on my tongue - if the seam so much as turns to follow you, the ground between us will learn it by heart! (Voice carrying after Kazuma, staff still ground into the seam.)
Go! Do not look back! I am planted in its path - let it spend every inch of its cold on my shield while you reach that light! (Shield braced, body set behind it, not looking back.)

Kazuma, do not turn back! The shade has already chosen the far wall — let my emptied hand and the wall's steel keep it honest, and run as if the gate will not wait! (Plants the staff against the seam a second time, chin high, eyes on the dark threading past.)

Go! If it will not spend its strength on me... then I will spend myself upon its hem and be dragged all the way to that light! (Steps into the shade's path, shield braced, breath short and white, one boot swallowed by the black hem.)

A costume-shop ghost?! I am a GODDESS holding open a graveyard gate with my bare divine hands, and all you can do is call me a disaster! If you had ever once believed in me, the undead would be too ashamed to even show their faces! (Still facing the gate, both wrists sunk in the seam; the light flares over her knuckles as she shouts, and the angel's head rocks in the crook of her arm.)

Kazuma, the seam under my staff is already crawling toward her light — stop trading insults with the glow and BE the wall between it and that gate! (Her voice carries thin over the frost from behind; the staff grounds again with a dull ring against the frozen row.)

Hold the seam? I have been holding this entire gate with my holy hands since before you even cleared the second row! 'Keep glowing,' he says - as if I am some cheap church lantern and not a goddess pouring her divine light into frozen iron! (Still facing the gate, both wrists buried in the seam; the light flares over her knuckles as she shouts.)

The seam is true while she holds it - but the shade is not! Kazuma, when she is through, seal that gate with everything the iron has left! (Voice carrying thin over the frost from behind; the staff rings against the frozen row.)

It has passed me... it means to swallow that light whole... let it drag me, then - I will be the dead weight that slows its black hem! (Breathless, stumbling after the shade's hem, shield still braced.)

Pull them through?! I am not some leaky bucket you can unplug and peer into, Kazuma! My hands are the only thing between that gate and the black hem, and you want me to pull them out for one second so you can see if the iron respects you more? It doesn't! It respects ME! (Does not turn; wrists still buried in the seam, the blue flaring over her knuckles as she shouts.)

The shade is no longer at the hem — it IS the hem, and it is closing faster than the two of you can argue! If she releases the seam now, the light goes with her hands and the dark will not need to chase anything at all! (Voice thin and carrying from behind; staff grounded against the frozen row.)

Let it have my boot... let it drag me over every stone between here and that gate... I will be the last warm thing it swallows before it reaches her light! (Breathless, stumbling after the shade's hem, shield braced.)

Let go of me! You tore me out of the seam and now the iron is sulking and the shade is at our heels — this is exactly what happens when you grab a goddess like a stuck drawer! (Half-turned by the Player's grip, one wrist still buried in the post, the freed hand flailing and streaming blue.)

The gate is holding with one hand, but the dark has stopped pretending to follow her light — it is following the hole she left! Kazuma, either put her back or pull her through, before that hole decides for you! (From behind, staff ringing against the frozen row as the shade's hem closes.)
Yes... pull her through and leave the seam gaping... let it pour over me until there is nothing left but the dent of my shield in the frost... (Breathless, stumbling toward the gate, shield braced.)

Thin?! My holy essence does not taste thin, you common little arsonist—it tastes like the beginning of the world, and that gate has been gulping it down like the first clean water it has ever had! It is not letting go because it is greedy, not because I am weak—and now that you have pulled half of me loose, it is angry, which is YOUR fault! (Half-turned in the Player's grip, the freed hand jabbing a blue finger toward his chest; the buried wrist flares as the seam pulls.)

The frost is turning to glass beneath it—the dark has a mouth now, and it is chewing toward the gate! Kazuma, if the seam is the true mouth, then shut it from the outside before it learns to swallow with two lips! (From behind, voice thin and carrying; the staff planted and ringing against the frozen row.)

If it must chew... let it chew through me... I will wedge myself into the hole and feel every iron tooth find my ribs while you watch— (Breathless, stumbling, shield braced against the black mirror spreading over the frost.)

It is not thin, you common little arsonist - it is gulping! It was sipping before you tore me half loose, and now it drinks like it has been thirsty for a hundred years! If I stop pouring, it will take the rest through my bones and then ask for you by name! (Half-turned in the Player's grip, the buried wrist flaring as the seam pulses; her freed hand scatters blue smoke.)

Upward—of course it pulls upward! I have been telling you it drinks me like a wick while you stand there touching my iron like you built it! Now hold it still so the greedy thing doesn't turn around and drink from the broken end you made! (Half-turned in the Player's grip, the buried wrist flaring as the seam pulses; her freed hand scatters blue smoke.)

The dark is not following her anymore—it has turned toward the place where your heat melts her frost! If the crown is the true mouth, then feed the mouth and do not let the seam learn to swallow with two lips! (From behind, staff ringing against the frozen row as the black hem pours over the meltwater.)

Let it climb... let the crown drink until it forgets the seam and comes looking for a throat it can close over mine... (Breathless, stumbling toward the gate, shield braced against the new ice spreading over the frost.)
It loosened! Did you see it loosen? Pull me free now, before it remembers which end is the meal and bites down again! (Wrenches her buried wrist, blue light flaring along the seam.)
The crown is the mouth now! One more pull of light and tear her free—do not let the dark learn to drink from both ends! (Staff ringing, voice carrying over the frost.)
If it must close over something... let it close over me, here, while you pry the goddess from its teeth— (Breathless, shield braced, one step closer.)

It let go! You see? You see? Even a greedy old gate knows a goddess cannot be chewed! Now shut it before it remembers my other wrist and comes back for a full set! (Wrenches her wrist free and cradles it, blue smoke hissing from her fingers.)

Kazuma, you did not burst it—you gave it a second lip! The crown is the throat now, and the seam is drinking air, and both of them are calling the dark to the gate! (Staff ringing against the frozen row, voice carrying over the cracking frost.)

Two lips, and neither has closed over me... How cruel... let me wedge myself into the seam while the iron is hot enough to know what it bites— (Stumbling closer, shield angled toward the widening seam.)

It's dying! Don't just stand there looking satisfied—finish it before it remembers I have two wrists and comes back for the matching set! (Cradling her freed wrist, blue smoke hissing between her fingers.)

The crown has cracked, but the seam is still open a finger's width! Strike the crown now, before the dark finds the second lip again! (Staff ringing against the frozen row as she steps over the slack black sheet.)

Let it close over the shield first... let it bite something it cannot chew through before the light leaves for good— (Shield angled toward the smoking seam, one boot sliding forward through the meltwater.)

See? Even a withered old gate knows better than to choke a goddess! Now shut it—shut it before it gets ideas about my other wrist—and then somebody find me something to drink! My fingers are still smoking! (Cradles her wrist, blue smoke hissing between her fingers.)

Do not mistake silence for surrender! The crown is cracked, but a mouth with a broken jaw can still close. Strike the seam now, Kazuma—one clean blow, while the dark is still blind and the second lip has not found its breath! (Steps over the slack black hem, staff ringing as it strikes the frozen row.)

If it will not close on its own... then let it close over my shield—nay, over my arm—while you hammer the crown shut! I can take the bite, Kazuma. I can take every tooth it has left. (Slides one boot forward through the meltwater, shield angled toward the smoking seam.)

snippets.text: Aqua continues purifying at the fourth row; the far gate still unseen; Kazuma commits to traveling, leaves Megumin and Darkness holding the line with Chunchunmaru freezing.
Kazuma's shout is swallowed without echo; he passes the black yew; frost thins to powder; the shade presses on the rear line but is left behind; Aqua's blue light waits unchanged at the far gate.
Kazuma turns back to shout at Aqua; black hem folds over Megumin's staff and Darkness's shield, Darkness's boot swallowed by the shade.

Aqua's light visible at the gate, still pulsing, not turning; Kazuma sees the gate as true iron, passes the rusted railing tooth and the peeled third row; he yells to Aqua not to close the gate, citing Megumin and Darkness holding the line.

Aqua’s wrists are sunk in the gate seam, feeding light up the scrollwork; Kazuma reaches her back as the gate rises taller than before; the shade pours forward, spreading frost and dragging wetly behind him; Megumin's staff rings; Aqua still hasn't turned.
Aqua's wrists sink into the gate seam, iron warm and sweet-smelling; seam drinks her light; shade advances along a new frost crack; Kazuma grabs her shoulder, forces one wrist free.

Aqua’s wrist pulls free, turning her toward Kazuma; gate readjusts its scrollwork to the remaining buried wrist; black hem closes over the last stones, Megumin’s staff rings three times, marking distance.

New elements: Kazuma plants hand flat on gate, feels heat/current; he identifies pale veins running to crown as the source—"tooth" up top; Aqua's freed hand streams blue nimbus; seam breathes; shade/black hem closes in, Darkness lurches, Megumin rings twice then stops; Kazuma commits to punching outside seam and orders Megumin to blow open the crown on his signal.
Kazuma's heat redirects iron flow upward; Aqua's light climbs to crown; vein knot smokes, sparks return; black hem turns frost to black glass mirror; Darkness nears, exposed meltwater refreezes.

The knot shines white-hot behind scrollwork; the gate shudders from third-row tooth to frozen path; seam slackens around Aqua’s wrist; blue light steams at the surface; black hem spreads as a slow shining sheet; Megumin’s staff splits dark but it knits shut; Darkness reaches the last leaning stone, shield scraping like knife on bone; hairline crack glows like live coal down crown; smell sharpens to scorched myrrh. Kazuma commands hold and collapses the tooth from inside.

After the yew-shade work and the sealing of the trench, the party returned to the guild, where Kazuma refused to accept that the cemetery was fully dead. He blamed Aqua's holy aura for drawing undead and ordered her back alone to purify every plot and row, pressing the gold-necked bottle into her numb hands; Aqua, furious and stung into proving herself, tucked the stone angel's head under her arm and marched into the frozen rows vowing to make every inch glow. Kazuma then followed her in with Megumin and Darkness, and when a shrouded shade broke from a split plot he shoved Aqua toward the far gate to go on alone and do goddess work. He, Megumin, and Darkness stayed to hold the shade, but the thing kept pouring after Aqua's light, and Kazuma has now committed to reaching her: he left Megumin and Darkness planted in its path and is running hard through the leaning stones toward the far gate, following Aqua's blue pulse. His shout goes ahead and does not come back; the blue at the far wall keeps its slow, even pulse over the gate iron, and the frost cracks like thin glass under his boots. Behind him Darkness is braced behind her shield and Megumin has her staff grounded, both calling after him to go and not look back. Ahead, Aqua has not looked back. She has driven deeper into the cemetery as ordered: the second row is finished, and she stepped over the rusted tooth of the old railing into the third row, where the frost peeled back before her sandal and a crawling shape folded flat into the light. That third row now smolders blue behind her as a clean corridor of steam. "We're broke BECAUSE you keep drinking," you mutter, but she's already flagging down the waitress for another round on your tab.

Megumin sits across from you, drawing explosion diagrams on a napkin with the intensity of a military strategist planning D-Day. She already went on her daily Explosion pilgrimage at dawn — you know because the distant boom rattled the mansion windows and woke you up. She's been unusable for combat since about 6 AM.

Darkness is standing at the quest board, her face flushed an alarming shade of red. She's found something. Given her expression — somewhere between terror and excitement — it probably involves monsters with tentacles.

"K-Kazuma," she stammers, not turning around. "There's a quest here for subjugating a nest of Brutal Alligators in the sewers. It says they... they grapple their prey and drag them underwater..."

She's trembling. That's not fear.

Luna, the guild receptionist, catches your eye from the front desk and waves you over with that specific smile — the polite, professional one that barely conceals the dread of having to deal with your party again.

I glance at Aqua, still sobbing into her mug, then back at Darkness practically vibrating at the quest board.

"Darkness — the cemetery's got undead piling up because of her goddess aura. You and Megumin hold down the guild. Aqua." I jerk my chin at her. "Get up. You're going to the cemetery to purify the undead you've been attracting. That's your job, so go do it — and don't come back until you've actually done it."

The hall holds its breath for half a second, then lets it out in a collective, practiced sigh. Aqua's finger is still aimed at you, trembling with the force of a complaint that has been rehearsed across three mugs and many ruined mornings. Darkness's hand has not quite come back down from where she reached for the board. Megumin grips the edge of the table to steady herself, as if standing is a tactical decision she is still negotiating.

None of them move toward the door. The cemetery, somewhere beyond the guild's warm windows, keeps its dead to itself for the moment.

I watch Aqua wag her finger at me, and I don't blink. I just let the silence stretch before I push my chair back and stand.

"Aqua." I grab her by the sleeve of her priestess robe and tug her toward the door. "You heard me. Cemetery. Undead. Purify. It's literally what you're for. One Healing spell and a prayer and you're a hero — stop wailing about mid-shelf and go earn it."

I point at her, then jerk my thumb at the door.

The chair scrapes back and the guild floor catches your weight. Your grip closes on the loose sleeve of Aqua's robe, and the fabric bunches as you pull her toward the door. She stumbles half a step, ale still sloshing in her mug, her free hand flying out for balance. The hall's practiced sigh thins into a murmur, then a circle of not-quite-hidden stares.

Near the quest board, Darkness lowers her hand by degrees, then raises it again as if volunteering for something terrible. Megumin stays at the table, chin high, both hands planted on the edge like a captain lashed to the mast of a listing ship. At the counter, Luna has stopped pretending to file papers; her smile is fixed in place.

You point at Aqua. The finger lands a breath from her nose. Beyond the doorway, the morning is bright enough to show every dust mote hanging in the air.

"Nobody's marching an army to the cemetery — just you, Aqua." I keep my grip on her sleeve and face her dead on. "You go alone. Purify the undead, mind the headstones, come back when it's done."

I turn to Darkness and Megumin before they can follow. "Both of you, stay. We've got the alligator quest to sort out, and I'm not paying bail for a goddess, a crusader, and a one-spell mage in the same morning."

I shove Aqua toward the door and hold up one finger. "One Healing prayer, tops. No theatrics. Go."

The second notice in Luna's hands is creased from being re-read too many times, and she does not look up as she speaks. Aqua's sleeve stays bunched in your fist, but her weight has shifted entirely to her heels, and the mug now hangs forgotten at her side, dripping into the groove between the flagstones. Behind you, Megumin's grip on the table has turned white-knuckled with the effort of looking ready.

I hold my ground, fist still bunched in her sleeve. "Both of you stay put." I cut a look at Darkness and Megumin. "Alligator quest's still on the board. I'm not chasing two disasters."

The shove carries Aqua to the threshold, and for one bright second her silhouette fills the open door, robe sleeves flaring, the mug swinging out in a wide arc that paints a thin crescent of ale across the flagstones. She catches herself against the doorframe with her free hand and clings there, half in the hall and half in the morning, glaring back at you with her face screwed up in a way that has the nearest table of adventurers leaning back as one.

Your fist stays bunched in her sleeve. The fabric strains between you, and she does not step outside. Behind you, Darkness has risen halfway out of her chair, caught between the cemetery she was refused and the marsh she has already begun to imagine. Megumin remains at the table like a general at a wobbly command post, chin lifted, one hand pressed flat to the wood. Luna watches the spilled ale spread along the grout and says nothing yet, but her smile has gone thin and fixed.
